newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria seeks to double wine exports to EU.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria seeks to double wine exports to EU.

text.p: Bulgaria will seek to double its wine exports to European Union member countries next year, Trade Minister Valentin Vasilev said on Thursday.
"We will seek to negotiate with the European Union to double quotas for export of wine in 1998," told reporters.
Wine export limits to the EU agreed for 1997 stood at 368,000 hectolitres of brand wine, at 128,000 hectolitres of unbottled wine and 1,500 hectolitres of sparkling wine, Vasilev said.
Bulgaria hopes next year to export 603,000 hectolitres of brand wine, 265,000 hectolitres of unbottled wine and 4,550 hectolitres of sparkling wine.
Bulgaria will also seek to reduce in 1998 customs duties levied by EU countries on wine by a further 20 percent, Vasilev said.
The EU agreed last year to reduce the customs duties levied on Bulgarian wine exports this year by 60 percent.
In return, Bulgaria will offer preferential conditions for EU imports of spirits like gin and Scotch, Vasilev said.
Bulgaria's wine industry is one of the few least affected by the country's tortuous transition to market economy and wine remains a major export item.
